purpose: Measured synthetic loopback TCP fixture; banners are simulated, not verified installed services. No live NVD or Juice Shop assessment.

findings.title: TCP listener accepted a connection
findings.description: A TCP handshake completed on this approved address and port. An open listener alone is not a vulnerability or evidence of an unauthenticated application action. Service identity is assessed separately.
findings.remediation: Review whether the listener is required, bind private services to the intended interface, restrict ingress with host/network firewalls, and enforce service authentication and patching.

findings.title: Passive service identity advertised
findings.description: A greeting matched a bounded built-in signature. Banners can be spoofed and distribution packages may backport fixes. No login, HTTP request, database query or service command was sent. [Needs manual verification] for installed product/version and vulnerability applicability.
findings.remediation: Verify installed package versions and vendor patch/backport status through authorized administrative inventory. Restrict unnecessary greeting detail, while prioritizing patching and access control over banner hiding.

findings.title: TCP response observed
findings.description: A connect succeeded or was refused. This establishes a response from the address/path, possibly a firewall or middlebox, not proof of end-host identity. No ICMP/raw SYN packet or application command was sent.

observations: Every authorized address remains eligible for selected-port probing regardless of this response.

findings.remediation: Maintain an accurate asset inventory and limit network exposure to the intended trust zones. Verify address ownership and any middlebox responses with the operator.

coverage.reason: No NVD cache configured; no external lookup was made.
